localVariables.note: CPU-RAM.ini's own [Variables] section only ADDS these two keys; it does not override any of the global Scale/BgOffset/Colors/etc. values supplied in the task prompt (verified directly against @Resources/Variables.inc - every value matches).

resolvedGlobalsUsedHere.deg: degree sign (U+00B0) via Rainmeter inline hex-char [\x0x00B0]

backgroundDetail.note: Uses the global StyleBackground unmodified (no per-meter geometry overrides in CPU-RAM.ini). Two-zone rounded rect: top title band (Shape/Shape2/Shape3 union, y=BgOffset..BgOffset+21ish scaled, fill BgTopColor 163,178,230/180) + body band (Shape4/Shape5/Shape6 union, fill BgBodyColor 230,230,230/180) + outline frame (Shape7, StrokeWidth=Stroke_Width*Scale=0, StrokeColor 96,138,203/100, so effectively invisible stroke since width 0), CornerRadius=4 (scaled). All coordinates pre-multiplied by #Scale#=1.7 inside the Shape strings themselves (in addition to the meter's own TransformationMatrix scale via H formula) - see notes.
backgroundDetail.widthFormula: (((#BgShapeW# + 0.06) + (#BgOffset# * 2)) * #Scale#) = ((196+0.06+10)*1.7) = 350.30 px (this W is already in final scaled px, unlike other meters which are given in unscaled 206-space and then scaled by TransformationMatrix)
backgroundDetail.heightFormula: ([MeterBackgroundHeight:Y] * #Scale#) - fully dynamic, grows with number of visible core rows and whether ShowGraph histograms are shown
backgroundDetail.heightDrivingMeter: MeterBackgroundHeight (Image, transparent, Y=(#BottomMargin#+#BgOffset#+2)R = 10R relative to the bottom of the last VISIBLE content meter in the R-chain)
backgroundDetail.heightEstimateShowGraph1: ~348 logical units (10R after meterHistogramAlign bottom=338, using the font-metric inference documented in notes) -> *1.7 = ~591.6 px
backgroundDetail.heightEstimateShowGraph0: ~319 logical units (10R after RamUsageBar bottom=309) -> *1.7 = ~542.3 px
backgroundDetail.caveat: StyleBackground's own Shape coordinate strings already multiply by #Scale#, and W/H are computed in already-scaled px, which is a deliberate exception to the 'meter uses TransformationMatrix to scale' pattern used by every other meter in this file. Report coordinates for THIS shape as already-scaled; all other meters in 'meters' below are reported UNSCALED (logical 206-wide space) per task instructions.

measures.name: MeasureRun

ifConditions.condition: (#CURRENTSECTION#>0) i.e. detected logical processor count > 0 (effectively always true)
ifConditions.effect: [!WriteKeyValue "Variables" "CPUCores" "[MeasureRun]" "#@#Variables.inc"] - persists the LIVE-detected logical processor count into Variables.inc as CPUCores. On the machine this skin instance was captured from, that resolved to 20 (i5-14600K = 6 P-cores x2 HT + 8 E-cores x1 = 20 logical processors).

measures.note: Not bound to any meter's MeasureName; purely a self-configuring side effect measure that keeps CPUCores in sync with the actual system. For a static re-implementation, CPUCores=20 can be treated as a fixed constant matching this captured profile.

measures.name: CPUPERCENTCALC

measures.name: MeasureSettingsScript

meters.name: MeterBackground
meters.notes: See top-level 'background'/'backgroundDetail' fields for full resolved geometry. First meter in file.

meters.name: meterTitle
meters.notes: Panel title, drawn once (UpdateDivider=-1).

meters.name: meterHideGraphs_
meters.fontFace: Trebuchet MS (inherited; glyph likely renders via a symbol/emoji fallback since char is U+23F6)
meters.text: [\x23F6]  (U+23F6 BLACK UP-POINTING DOUBLE TRIANGLE - 'collapse graphs' icon)
meters.notes: Visible only while ShowGraph=1. Mutually exclusive with meterShowGraphs_ (same X/Y, opposite Hidden condition) - together they form one toggle icon at the top-right of the panel, next to the title.

meters.name: meterShowGraphs_
meters.text: [\x0x23F7]  (U+23F7 BLACK DOWN-POINTING DOUBLE TRIANGLE - 'expand graphs' icon)
meters.notes: Visible only while ShowGraph=0 (graphs collapsed).

meters.name: CPUTotalTemp
meters.fontColor: [MCPUTempCalc] (dynamic; see MCPUTempCalc ifConditions - one of the 5 DevTempWarnColorTh1..5 colors)
meters.notes: Absolute Y=30, centered under the title - the lone CPU package-temperature reading. No explicit H; not chained-into by anything else so its auto-height is inconsequential.

meters.name: CpuCoresUsageText
meters.notes: No explicit H (Rainmeter auto-measures text height for this FontSize=8 Bold string). Its bottom feeds CPUTotalBarGraphUsage's R-relative Y - see top-level notes on the auto-height inference (=11).

meters.name: CpuCoresUsagePercent
meters.notes: Same row as CpuCoresUsageText (Y=r). Last non-hidden meter before CPUTotalBarGraphUsage, so its (inferred) bottom = 32+11 = 43 anchors the bar.

meters.name: CPUTotalBarGraphUsage
meters.notes: Y=0R means flush against the (inferred) bottom of CpuCoresUsagePercent - i.e. no gap between the 'CPU: NN%' text row and this 1px bar underneath it.

meters.name: MeterCpuUsageRowAdjustor
meters.notes: Fully invisible spacer meter (alpha 0) that exists purely to correct the vertical flow: it rewinds the Y cursor by 12 logical units (one full core-row pitch) so that Core1UsageText begins at the same Y as CPUTotalBarGraphUsage rather than a full row below it. When CpuUsage=0 this meter (and the whole CPU-total block) is Hidden, so per Rainmeter's Hidden-skipping R/r resolution, Core1UsageText's chain instead walks back to whatever the last visible meter was (CPUTotalTemp/title/etc.) with zero extra offset. This -12 value is the strongest evidence that the auto (no-H) line height for FontSize=8 text in this skin is intended to be 11 (matching the explicit H=11 used by styleSecondaryText2), since 12 = RowSpacing(1) + assumed-lineheight(11).

meters.name: Core1UsageText
meters.notes: First per-core row. Row pitch for cores 2-20 is a clean, deterministic 12 logical units (H=11 explicit + RowSpacing=1) since styleSecondaryText2 fixes H=11; only this row's anchor to the CPU-total block above is inferred (see MeterCpuUsageRowAdjustor).

meters.name: Core11UsageText
meters.notes: Bar+percent for cores 11-20 follow the identical pattern shown for cores 1-10 above (X=47/W=120/H=1 bar at Y=CoreNUsageText.Y+7; percent text at X=197,Y=[CoreNUsageText:Y]); listed compactly below to avoid repeating the same structure 20 times over.

meters.name: Core12UsageText
meters.notes: LAST of the P-core rows (bars 1-12 correspond to the 6 physical P-cores' 12 hyperthreaded logical processors, per task framing).

meters.name: Core13UsageText
meters.notes: FIRST of the E-core rows (bars 13-20 -> 8 E-cores, per task framing).

meters.name: Core20UsageText
meters.notes: LAST visible core row on this 20-logical-processor profile. Core21..Core36 template rows follow identically in the file (Text='Core 21:'..'Core 36:', groups Core21..Core36) but are permanently Hidden/Disabled since cpuCores is fixed at 20 - see top-level 'skipped' and notes. Per Rainmeter's Hidden-skipping R/r resolution, MeterMHz's R-relative Y below correctly anchors to THIS row's bottom, not to any of the 16 hidden rows in between.

meters.name: MeterMHz

y.relativeTo: CPU20UsagePercent bottom (last visible core row; hidden Core21-36 rows are skipped by Rainmeter's R resolution)

meters.notes: StringStyle explicitly set to Normal (not bold, though styleSecondaryText doesn't set Bold anyway). Carries an explicit SolidColor (248,248,248,255, near-white) and full ContentWidth (190) - this draws a filled label 'chip' background rectangle spanning the whole row width behind BOTH the Clock text (left) and the Fan text (right, same row) since CPUFanText shares the same Y and has no competing SolidColor of its own.

meters.name: CPUFanText
meters.notes: Same visual row as MeterMHz: 'Clock: NNNN MHz' left, 'FAN: NNNNrpm' right.

meters.name: RAMUsedGB
meters.notes: %2=MeasureRAMUsed (Used), %1=MeasureRAMTotal (Total); template renders as 'Used/Total'. %3 (MeasureRAMFree) is bound but never referenced in the Text template - a dead measure slot. Autoscale=1 makes Rainmeter scale the raw byte counts and insert a K/M/G/T magnitude letter; the literal 'B' characters in the template complete the unit (e.g. produces '16.0GB/32.0GB').

meters.name: RamUsagePercent
meters.notes: Percentual=1: displays MeasureRAMUsed as a percentage of total physical memory rather than raw bytes.

meters.name: meterHistogram
meters.notes: Purely a translucent white background panel (SolidColor=EmptyBarColor) behind the three overlaid line-graph meters that follow; not itself a graph.

meters.name: CpuTempHistogram
meters.notes: LineColor overridden to #CpuTempColor# (204,0,0), overriding StyleGraph's default colorHistogram (176,196,222).

meters.name: CpuUsageHistogram
meters.notes: LineColor overridden to #CpuUsageColor# (176,196,222) - coincidentally identical to StyleGraph's default colorHistogram value, so visually unchanged from the style default.

meters.name: RamUsageHistogram
meters.notes: LineColor overridden to #RamUsageColor# (102,204,0). All three line graphs (CPU temp red, CPU usage light-blue, RAM usage green) render overlaid in the exact same 8,Y,188x25 rect, sharing meterHistogram's translucent-white backdrop - i.e. a single combined multi-series line chart, not three stacked charts.

meters.name: meterHistogramAlign
meters.notes: Fully transparent (alpha 0) Image meter, same rect as the graph. Appears to serve only as a stable, always-present 'last meter of the GraphsMeter group' anchor for MeterBackgroundHeight's R-chain (so the background sizing calc has a consistent, group-tagged meter to fall back through), rather than drawing anything itself.

meters.name: MeterBackgroundHeight

y.relativeTo: last VISIBLE meter in the chain: meterHistogramAlign (ShowGraph=1) or RamUsageBar (ShowGraph=0)

meters.notes: Invisible marker meter whose Y (not bottom) is read back by StyleBackground's H formula ([MeterBackgroundHeight:Y] * #Scale#) to size the rounded-rect background panel dynamically. A commented-out alternate formula in the file '((2 * (#ShowGraph#=1)?) + #BottomMargin# + #BgOffset# + 0)R' was abandoned in favor of the simpler active one.

verticalFlowSummary: Background: rounded-rect panel (Shape meter), dynamic height, drawn first/behind everything.
Title row (abs Y=9): CPU name/model, centered, uppercase, bold.
Top-right toggle icon (abs Y=4, X=197): collapse/expand graphs (mutually exclusive pair).
CPU temp row (abs Y=30): single centered '<temp>°C' reading, color-coded by warning threshold.
CPU total usage row (abs Y=32): 'CPU:' label left, '<pct>%' right, both same Y.
CPU total usage bar (Y=0R, flush under the row above): thin 1px full-width bar, color-coded >75% warning.
[invisible row-adjustor spacer, rewinds cursor by one row-pitch]

Core 1..Core 20 rows (12-unit pitch each): 'Core N:' label left (X=7) + '<pct>%' right (X=197) on one text line, with a short 1px usage bar (X=47,W=120) positioned 7 units below the row's start, inset under the text. Rows 1-12 = P-cores (12 logical processors from 6 HT-enabled P-cores), rows 13-20 = E-cores (8 logical processors, no HT).
Clock/Fan row: 'Clock: NNNN MHz' left (on a subtle near-white background chip spanning the row) + 'FAN: NNNNrpm' right, same Y.
RAM row: 'RAM:' label left, 'usedGB/totalGB' centered, '<pct>%' right, all same Y; thin 1px usage bar underneath, color-coded >75% warning.
Graph area (only if ShowGraph=1): translucent backdrop rectangle (188x25) with three overlaid line graphs (CPU temp red, CPU usage light-blue/lavender, RAM usage green) sharing the same plot rect.
[invisible background-height marker, closes out the content flow]
notes: PRIMARY CAVEAT - auto text height inference: styleFirstLineText, stylePrimaryText, and styleSecondaryText (used by CPUTotalTemp, CpuCoresUsageText/Percent, MeterCpuUsageRowAdjustor, MeterMHz, CPUFanText, RamUsageLabel/RAMUsedGB/RamUsagePercent) do NOT set an explicit H - Rainmeter auto-measures the string's rendered height. Only styleSecondaryText2 (the per-core label/percent style) explicitly fixes H=11. All 'resolvedAbsolute_inferred' Y values in this JSON assume an effective line-height of 11 logical units for FontSize=8 text in this configuration, an inference drawn from internal evidence in the file itself (the MeterCpuUsageRowAdjustor's '-12' = RowSpacing(1)+11 correction, deliberately designed to make Core1 line up flush with the CPU-total bar). This should be verified/corrected against actual Rainmeter DirectWrite metrics for 'Trebuchet MS' at 8pt (and 9pt for the title) if exact pixel parity is required; every meter whose Y is a plain formula (no 'resolvedAbsolute_inferred' tag) is exact/deterministic given the constants already supplied.

PRIMARY CAVEAT - Hidden-skipping relative layout: Rainmeter's Y/X '...R'/'...r' relative-position resolution walks back to the nearest NON-hidden preceding meter, skipping any meter whose Hidden evaluates true. This is essential (and not stated anywhere in the .ini itself) to correctly collapse: (a) the always-disabled Core21-Core36 template rows so MeterMHz sits directly under Core20 rather than 16 empty rows further down, and (b) any of the CpuTemp/CpuUsage/CpuCoresUsage/CpuClockFan/RamUsage/ShowGraph toggle sections if a re-implementation exposes those as user-configurable (they are all '=1' i.e. all visible in this captured profile, so this concern is latent, not currently manifesting).

Two distinct 'normal' bar colors: the aggregate CPU-total bar's non-warning color is CpuUsageColor (176,196,222), while every individual per-core bar's non-warning color is the separate 'colorBar' constant (93,141,172) - confirmed directly from the two different Substitute strings (CPUBARWARNT vs CPUBARWARN1-20). The RAM bar's non-warning color is RamUsageColor (102,204,0). All three share the same warning color/threshold: >75% -> crimson 220,20,60 @ alpha 200.
RAMUsedGB's MeasureName3 (MeasureRAMFree) is bound but never referenced by a %3 token in its Text template - effectively a dead/unused measure slot for this specific meter.
Autoscale=1 on RAMUsedGB only affects that one meter; RamUsagePercent instead uses Percentual=1 (percentage-of-max display, not byte scaling).

MeterMHz carries an explicit SolidColor (248,248,248 @ 255) and W=ContentWidth(190), producing a full-row-width near-white 'chip' background rendered behind both the Clock (left) and Fan (right) text on that row; no other text meter in this panel has a SolidColor.

StyleBackground's own Shape coordinate strings are pre-multiplied by #Scale# internally (in addition to sitting inside a TransformationMatrix-scaled meter), which is different from every other meter in the file (which are unscaled/logical and rely solely on the shared TransformationMatrix). Per the task's instruction to report coordinates unscaled, all NON-background meters above are given in the logical 206-wide space; the background shape's own internal formulas are called out explicitly as an exception in 'backgroundDetail'.

No skin-local [Variables] overrides of the given global Scale/BgOffset/margins/colors/CPU-RAM-specific constants were found; CPU-RAM.ini's own [Variables] section only adds CPUName and ShowGraph=1 on top of the three @Include directives.
The degree symbol and 'C' unit suffix come from the shared #deg# (Rainmeter inline hex-char escape for U+00B0) and #TempUnitLetter# variables, not literal text in this file.

Rainmeter Update=1000ms (global); most measures/meters update every tick (UpdateDivider unset/1) except MeasureRAMUsed (UpdateDivider=2, i.e. every 2s) and everything with UpdateDivider=-1 (draw-once: title, static labels, background geometry, hide/show icon meters, MeasureRAMTotal, MeasureSettingsScript).
